scope: Architecture and failure-mode assessment. No application code changes. Other sessions were editing UI/domain files during review; hashes record key source versions at report creation.
conclusion: Retain PowerSync. The most urgent gaps are in our upload/session/context contracts and integration coverage, rather than the replication transport.

architecture.web: @powersync/web with persistent clientbridge.db; shared app-core reactive SQL; browser token storage and a Web Lock around refresh.
architecture.ios_and_android: One React Native implementation using @powersync/react-native, native SQLite, SecureStore tokens, the same shared connector and app-core queries.
architecture.connect: Public HTTP endpoints with scoped capability/verification flows; no application PowerSync replica.
architecture.marketing_and_playground: Static/generated examples and component previews; not business-data replication clients.
architecture.download: Postgres WAL -> PowerSync source replication -> powersync_storage bucket state -> authorized token stream -> local SQLite -> reactive useQuery views.
architecture.upload: Recurring hours local write transaction -> persistent CRUD queue -> shared connector -> authenticated /sync/upload -> server ownership validation and commit -> queue acknowledgement -> authoritative rows return through replication.
architecture.commands: Bookings, money, clients and other invariants use HTTP commands, not offline CRUD. Local device preferences never upload. Reports and notifications include server reads.
architecture.authentication: 15-minute access token -> /sync/token -> one-hour PowerSync token. Shared authFetch retries after 401 via a rotating 30-day refresh session.
architecture.authorization: Shared business bucket, limited staff projection, own staff rows and owner/admin full bucket. Active membership governs read replication; API services and upload policy separately govern writes.
architecture.schema: Generated from backend model types and table names in sync rules: 35 synced tables plus device_prefs. Backend indexes are mirrored, not independently tuned to all SQLite query patterns.

strengths: Shared web/native connector and domain queries
Narrow offline write surface keeps financial invariants server authoritative
Tenant/role-filtered streams; separate upload ownership and concurrency guards
Single-flight refresh and web refresh lock
Explicit sign-out warns about queued work
Generated schema and strong existing backend test coverage

findings.title: A replayed upload can permanently block the upload queue
evidence: backend/src/clientbridge/sync/upload.py:104 returns 403 when DELETE target no longer exists
frontend/packages/sync/src/connector.ts:39 throws on every non-2xx and never completes the transaction
Rollback-isolated API probe: insert 200, first delete 200, repeated delete 403; connector probe: two 403 attempts, zero completions
findings.impact: If the server commits a recurring-hours replacement but its response is lost, replay starts with already-deleted IDs and cannot complete. Later queued edits remain behind it. Pending writes can also delay application of downloaded checkpoints.
findings.recommendation: Give upload transactions stable client/device operation IDs and persist their results atomically with writes. Replay the recorded result. Treat authorized already-applied deletes as successful where safe; a blind no-op delete alone is not enough to replay a whole replacement transaction. Distinguish retryable failures from permanent validation or permission rejections, preserve a recoverable rejected-change record, and reconcile the local optimistic state before acknowledging a permanent rejection.
acceptance: Drop HTTP response after database commit and replay: exactly one logical change, queue drains
Queue a forbidden edit then an allowed edit: show the rejection and allow recovery without discarding silently
Test permission loss while hours changes are offline

findings.title: The upload endpoint does not validate working-hours shape
evidence: backend/src/clientbridge/sync/upload.py:20 accepts unbounded generic ops/data
backend/src/clientbridge/sync/upload.py:41 uses bool(value) and direct ISO parsing
backend/src/clientbridge/models/scheduling.py:100 only constrains exception windows and staff presence
API probe accepted weekday=42 and start=17:00,end=09:00 with 200; string false stored true; malformed time and unknown column returned 500
findings.impact: Invalid schedules can reach the authoritative database. Malformed requests become server errors and are retried by the connector.
findings.recommendation: Use a typed hours mutation schema with a writable-column allowlist, strict booleans, weekday bounds, basis-specific required fields and ordered time windows. Merge PATCH with the locked row before validating. Limit operation count/body size and return structured 422 errors. Mirror durable invariants with database checks after auditing existing rows.
acceptance: Reject invalid weekdays, reversed/missing windows, unsupported columns and ambiguous booleans with 422
Invalid operation rolls back the entire batch
An accepted local hours edit remains compatible with the typed API

findings.status: confirmed code path plus conditional failure probe
findings.title: Refresh failure can destroy unsynced work
evidence: frontend/packages/api-client/src/session.ts:63 clears credentials and calls onSignedOut for refresh 401/403
Both application roots call disconnectAndClear for automatic and explicit sign-out
backend/src/clientbridge/services/auth.py:119 revokes old refresh tokens on rotation and treats replay as family compromise
Session probe simulated loss of an already-rotated response: first attempt retains old token, second signs out
findings.impact: A lost rotation response, revoked session or demo reset can lead to automatic replica/queue deletion without the explicit sign-out pending-work prompt. This is a possible cause of idle/reconnect trouble, not a diagnosis of the previously reported device incident.
findings.recommendation: Separate reauthentication-required from explicit discard/sign-out. Disconnect and lock the replica to its existing user, preserve queued work, reauthenticate that same user and reconcile; never expose it to a different user. Make refresh rotation safely retryable using an explicit request identifier or tightly bounded, device-bound replay design with stored replacement results. Keep reuse detection; do not simply disable it.
acceptance: Expire access token with valid refresh: silent recovery
Drop refresh response after commit: safe bounded retry
Revoke session with pending hours: retain locked changes and show recovery
Login as a different user never sees or uploads old-user changes

findings.title: Session and replica lifecycle is not coordinated across browser tabs
evidence: Web token storage is shared localStorage, guarded only for refresh by navigator.locks
frontend/apps/web/src/App.tsx keeps authentication in per-tab React state
No app-level storage/BroadcastChannel handler coordinates login/logout; each platform uses clientbridge.db
Session recover treats any changed access token as a successful refresh without checking user identity
findings.impact: A second tab can remain in the old authenticated state after logout or account change. A late refresh can race sign-out and persist tokens again. Requests in flight may retry under a changed session. Precise cross-tab behavior still needs browser reproduction; SDK database locks do not implement the application auth state machine.
findings.recommendation: Centralize an auth generation and user binding, coordinate token writes/login/logout/refresh under one session lock, notify tabs, cancel stale requests and reject cross-generation responses. Serialize connection/clear/login transitions. Bind the database or its metadata to environment and user; distinguish authentication changes from ordinary token rotation.
acceptance: Two tabs, concurrent refresh, logout during refresh, and login as another user
Reload/crash between credential clearing and database clearing
Exactly one active session identity and no stale-token resurrection

findings.title: Multiple memberships produce mixed local context
evidence: infra/powersync/sync-rules.yaml syncs every active membership
frontend/packages/app-core/src/domain/business.ts uses businesses LIMIT 1
frontend/packages/app-core/src/domain/auth.ts uses staff by user LIMIT 1
Client and other list queries lack an active business filter
backend/src/clientbridge/core/deps.py requires X-Business-Id for multi-business users; shared client does not consistently attach one
findings.impact: A legitimately multi-business user can see combined lists with an arbitrary brand/role context, while API commands reject ambiguous business selection. This is a client context gap, not proof that an unauthorized business is replicated.
findings.recommendation: Choose an explicit product contract: support a selected business throughout local SQL, role resolution, command headers, pending edits and navigation, or enforce single membership consistently. Keep selected business as a narrowing filter, never as the authority granting sync access.
acceptance: One user belongs to A and B with different roles; lists, totals, logos and commands agree
Switch business with pending edits
Unrelated C remains absent from the local database

findings.title: Read authorization rules are not tested through a real sync service in CI
evidence: Existing backend sync tests cover token and upload endpoints
CI provisions Postgres/object storage but no PowerSync service; Connect browser tests use public HTTP routes
Local SQLite query tests do not execute sync-rules.yaml
findings.impact: An error in bucket membership, limited staff projections or revocation can ship even while backend authorization tests pass.
findings.recommendation: Add a pinned Postgres + PowerSync + actual SDK integration harness. Assert rows and sensitive columns at the local replica, not just server responses. Keep public/admin tokens, financial fields, membership removal and role downgrade in the test matrix.
acceptance: Owner/admin/staff/contractor/removed-member and multi-business fixtures
Foreign-tenant rows absent; staff pay columns and server-only tables absent
Online role downgrade removes prior full projections
Offline removal/reconnect behavior explicitly documented and tested

findings.title: Recurring hours are a delete-and-reinsert aggregate without conflict control
evidence: frontend/packages/app-core/src/domain/hours.ts:207 deletes all recurring rows and allocates fresh IDs
No aggregate revision or stable weekday identity is sent
findings.impact: Two devices editing the same old week can conflict on deleted IDs; treating missing deletes as no-ops alone can leave duplicate replacement schedules. Empty-baseline concurrent inserts can also coexist.
findings.recommendation: Model a staff week as a versioned aggregate with stable entries and an atomic replace operation. Preserve offline capability with a queued domain envelope if required; return the current version and a clear conflict choice. Select and document merge semantics instead of relying on row last-write-wins.
acceptance: Two devices edit the same baseline offline and reconnect in both orders
Exactly one valid schedule or an explicit resolvable conflict; no duplicate week
Response-loss replay is safe with S01

findings.title: Sync status hides upload failures and initial connection errors
evidence: frontend/packages/app-core/src/domain/sync.ts exposes connected/hasSynced but not uploadError/downloadError
getCrudBatch(50) is presented as the total pending count
Mobile offline banner is on Today, not the app shell
Both roots swallow connectPowerSync rejection; mobile SecureStore-read rejection leaves authed null
useReplicaLoad waits on hasSynced without a transport error source
findings.impact: A connected downloader with a blocked uploader can appear healthy. A first-run failure can look like indefinite loading. Large queues are undercounted and authentication, API and transport outages are indistinguishable.
findings.recommendation: Expose a shared sync-health state with separate auth, API, download, upload, first-sync and stale-data states. Report true queue count plus a bounded preview and oldest pending age. Render recovery actions globally; label connected separately from internet available. Add bounded initialization and visible storage failures.
acceptance: Connected plus upload 403 produces action-required state
First sync while API or PowerSync is unavailable shows retryable error
More than 50 pending operations report an accurate total
Diagnostics redact tokens and personal payloads

findings.title: Remote commands and local replica reads have an unmodeled catch-up interval
evidence: Most business actions POST directly to the API while their resulting views read useQuery from SQLite
No shared row-observation/catch-up utility or checkpoint request mode was found
hasSynced records completed initial sync, not freshness after the latest command
findings.impact: A successful create, payment, notification tap or refresh may lead to a row or balance that has not arrived locally yet. A generic sync-success flag cannot prove read-your-write consistency.
findings.recommendation: Use command response data for the immediate success view, then observe the expected row/version with timeout and cancellation. Evaluate PowerSync checkpoint requests for a general catch-up barrier only after version and failure tests; the current upstream feature is alpha. Keep offline read availability instead of blocking all views behind freshness.
acceptance: Artificial CDC delay after successful commands
Open notification before its row arrives
Bounded wait gives useful pending state and cannot hang indefinitely

findings.title: Replica size and query result size are unbounded
evidence: Owner buckets sync all historical ledger entries, invoices, payments, messages and bookings
Staff shared bucket includes all client records and messages
Several lists hydrate complete SQLite result sets before client-side filtering/slicing
findings.impact: As businesses grow, initial sync, local storage, reactive queries and JS rendering grow together. UI infinite scrolling alone does not reduce replicated data.
findings.recommendation: Measure cold sync and query plans at realistic multi-year volumes. Separate hot offline datasets, aggregates and on-demand historical detail. Add keyset pagination and virtualization to local lists and pagination to remote-only reads. Use Sync Streams/on-demand subscriptions where appropriate, preserving report correctness when history is not local.
acceptance: Define and meet cold-start, replica-size and list-latency budgets
Large clients/messages/ledger fixtures
Explicit offline availability and retention behavior for historical data

findings.title: Replication and database privilege are development-grade
evidence: Makefile creates FOR ALL TABLES publication and hides provisioning errors
PowerSync source and storage use clientbridge credentials
Live local role clientbridge is superuser and replication-enabled; no public table has RLS enabled
docker-compose.yml uses PowerSync latest without a dedicated healthcheck
findings.impact: The local setup is convenient, but is not a deployable least-privilege/observable production configuration. PostgreSQL RLS alone would not define PowerSync client read authorization.
findings.recommendation: Pin the PowerSync image, separate backend application, replication reader and storage roles, grant only documented privileges, scope publication appropriately, fail clearly on provisioning errors and monitor readiness/replication lag/WAL retention. Add backend RLS as defense in depth using non-bypass roles if adopting it, while retaining independently tested sync authorization.
acceptance: Least-privilege service boots, snapshots and streams
Replication stalls trigger alerts before WAL fills disk
Schema and service upgrade/rollback rehearsed
Do not drop powersync_storage: it is required bucket storage

findings.title: JWT revocation and production signing need an explicit policy
evidence: Access tokens live 15 minutes; PowerSync tokens one hour
/sync/token validates JWT but does not consult the session/user table or token type
Production settings do not require stable RS256 key configuration
An absent RS256 PEM falls back to process-local generated keys
findings.impact: Session logout/revocation does not immediately invalidate already-issued JWTs. Membership changes are separately reflected through sync rules, but an offline client retains already-downloaded data. Multi-worker ephemeral signing keys would produce inconsistent production verification.
findings.recommendation: Validate token purpose and user/session validity before minting sync credentials, define bounded revocation expectations, require durable production keys/JWKS with rotation, and test the production configuration. Do not promise remote erasure of an offline device; define its local lock/retention policy.
acceptance: Revoked session cannot mint new credentials under the chosen policy
Signing keys survive worker restarts and rotate with overlap
Removed member gets no new data once rule changes reach sync
Offline cached-data behavior matches explicit policy

findings.status: confirmed broad projections; access policy review required
findings.title: Broad SELECT star projections can expand the data sent to devices
evidence: Most sync rule data queries use SELECT *
Synced models contain capability links/provider references and shared personal data
Schema generation emits all model columns for detected tables even if a role receives a limited projection
findings.impact: Adding a backend column can silently expand a broad sync projection. Capability tokens may be intentional workflow data but need explicit audience approval. Generated local columns do not themselves prove that values are synced.
findings.recommendation: Maintain an allowlisted per-role sync data contract. Keep secrets/session material server-only and retrieve narrowly authorized public-share links through commands where needed. Add projection tests and schema-change review for newly added sensitive columns.
acceptance: A synthetic newly added sensitive column is not automatically exposed
Audit each capability URL and shared financial/personal field by role
Validate sparse staff projections separately from full admin schema

findings.title: Offline device data and attachments need explicit guarantees
evidence: No application-level SQLite encryption or browser persistence request configured in database constructors
Mobile tokens use SecureStore while web uses localStorage
File metadata syncs, but file bytes use presigned HTTP uploads/downloads with no durable attachment queue
findings.impact: Offline availability covers synced rows, not necessarily images, documents or unfinished uploads. Browser eviction and lost/shared devices need a defined recovery/privacy policy; platform storage protection may exist but was not verified here.
findings.recommendation: Document offline/read-only versus online-command capabilities. Evaluate native encrypted SQLite and browser storage persistence with platform tests, define logout/reauth retention, and add durable attachment caching/upload recovery only for required offline file workflows.
acceptance: Airplane-mode walkthrough states exactly which actions work
Cold restart, browser eviction and low disk space tests
File upload interruption can retry without orphaned user workflow

findings.title: Sync Rules should be migrated to supported Sync Streams
evidence: Current configuration uses bucket_definitions
Official September 22, 2026 announcement deprecates Sync Rules while keeping them supported today
Upstream migration can preserve current authorization with auto_subscribe streams
findings.impact: Continuing on unpinned latest risks a future incompatible service update. Migration is planned maintenance, not an immediate outage or reason to rewrite sync.
findings.recommendation: Pin the current service first, establish replica authorization tests, migrate to edition 3 streams preserving row sets and column visibility, then add on-demand history as a separate change. Test timestamp compatibility changes and the one-time resync.
acceptance: Parity of owner/staff/multi-business rows and columns
Older released clients reconnect successfully
One-time resync does not lose queued writes
Schedule before upstream removal/support deadlines

findings.title: Refresh requests have no application timeout or comprehensive client regression suite
evidence: createSession fetch calls do not provide an application timeout/AbortSignal
A shared pending refresh promise gates concurrent recovering requests
No dedicated session/connector tests exist in the API client and sync packages; current sync.test.ts covers labels
findings.impact: A request that never settles can stall multiple callers. Existing backend endpoint tests cannot verify the client recovery and lifecycle behavior that produced the observed logs.
findings.recommendation: Add bounded, cancellable auth requests and distinct failure reasons, with single-flight refresh tests and connector fault injection. Test mobile foreground/reconnect and browser multi-tab behavior against the installed SDK; do not assume the SDK lacks its own reconnect handling.
acceptance: Hung refresh releases waiting callers with a recoverable state
Concurrent 401s perform one refresh
Network/5xx preserves credentials; true revocation requires reauth
Real iOS/Android background and network transition tests

validation.upload_probe: Real FastAPI app and PostgreSQL via rollback-only outer transaction; no test rows persisted
validation.session_probe: Actual createSession and connector modules under a controlled transport; simulated lost refresh response signs out on retry, repeated permanent upload rejection does not complete queue entry
validation.infrastructure: Earlier HTTP readiness checks passed; replication slot active with 656 bytes retained at sample time. This is a point-in-time check, not an operational SLA. Local clientbridge role is superuser/replication-enabled; public RLS table count was zero.
not_run: Native at-rest encryption or OS backup verification

implementation_order.title: Protect queued edits and make uploads retry-safe
implementation_order.exit: Lost responses, concurrent offline edits and rejected operations cannot silently lose work or block forever.

implementation_order.title: Unify session lifecycle and business context
implementation_order.exit: Idle, foreground, revoked sessions, multi-tab and multi-membership have explicit tested behavior.

implementation_order.title: Expose health and read-after-command progress
implementation_order.exit: Users can distinguish saved locally, uploaded, caught up, stale and action required.

implementation_order.title: Test the actual replication security boundary
implementation_order.exit: CI executes real PowerSync with role/tenant/column/revocation assertions.

implementation_order.title: Harden operations and migrate configuration
implementation_order.exit: Pinned least-privilege deployment, lag monitoring and tested Streams parity.

implementation_order.title: Set scalability and offline-data guarantees
implementation_order.exit: Measured data budgets, deliberate retention, paginated views and documented offline file behavior.

upstream_sources.note: Deprecated now but supported; new major removes Rules September 15, 2027; support ends December 15, 2027. Migration and timestamp compatibility need review.
Preserve existing authorization semantics before adopting selective replication.
Alpha catch-up API; requires Service >=1.24.0 and explicit opt-in. hasSynced does not prove current freshness.
Web SDK has its own multi-tab machinery; application auth coordination is a separate concern.
